text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Parliament speaker Ilga Kreituse was sacked on the initiative of her own Democratic Party Saimnieks (DPS) from which she has also been dismissed. She was replaced as speaker by DPS deputy Alfred Chepanis and one of the deputy speakers. His post was taken by Aigar Jirgens, from the right-wing party, Fatherland & Freedom.

- Some 500 students held a picket near parliament, protesting against a bill on army service for students. The bill was not adopted at its third reading. President Ulmanis said he will meet the students next week.

- A Latvian delegation headed by Finance Minister Aivar Kreituss will take part in the IMF/World Bank meeting in Washington. Kreituss will adress the meeting on behalf of the three Baltic States. The Latvian delegation will include Minister of Economics Guntars Krasts, Minister of State Revenues Aija Pocha and central bank chief Einar Repshe.
- Parliament voted to send a new Latvian unit to Bosnia as part of the Swedish batallion.

- Murdered businessman Valery Machugin and his girlfriend Natalija Meisane were buried yesterday, attended by leading business figures. Police say the killing could be linked to that of Igor Conda, involved in the construction of a large supermarket on the outskirts of Riga.
- The Council of Europe issued a series of stamps devoted to President Ulmanis' speech at the Council's recent session.
- Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs acknowledged Latvia is not ready to join NATO among the first applicants. Nevertheless, he reassured on Latvia's will to be admitted to the alliance.
- The finance ministry wants to cut spending on education. As a result, teachers will not receive sickness allowances and their salaries will not be increased.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele was satisfied by the results of his visit to the USA.
- The transport ministry is drafting a bill which provides that private companies will be given the concession of building and operating motorways in some parts of Latvia.

- South Korea's Hyundai has started building a new series of liquid natural gas carrier ships for the Latvian Shipping Company. The ships will bear the names of Latvia's districts: the first will be called Kurzeme and the second Vidzeme.
- United Arab Emirate representatives said during a trip to Latvia that they are interested in opening air traffic between the UAE and the Baltics.
